question:
Select the option that can be used as a one word substitute for the given group of words.

An often-imaginary place or state of utter perfection and happiness
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Utopia"** refers to an often-imaginary place or state of utter perfection and happiness. (आदर्श लोक या स्थिति)

 
 
• **Example:** Many philosophers have written about their vision of a **utopia** where everyone lives in harmony.
 
 
 
• **"Utopia"** embodies the concept of a perfect society, free from the troubles and sufferings of the real world. (आदर्श समाज)
 
 
• **Example:** In her book, the author describes a **utopia **where there is no poverty or crime.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Inferno** (नरक): A place or state resembling hell, especially in terms of fire or intense heat.

 
 
• **Example:** The building was an inferno, with flames reaching high into the sky.
 
 
 
• **Dystopia** (दुःस्वप्न): An imagined place or state where everything is unpleasant or bad, typically a totalitarian or environmentally degraded society.
 
 
• **Example:** The novel is set in a dystopia where the government controls every aspect of life.
 
 
 
• **Euphoria** (आनंद): A feeling or state of intense excitement and happiness.
 
 
• **Example:** He was in a state of euphoria after winning the championship.
 
 

40:Tb64,

The correct answer is: **Option 1.**
